name: Gorvokk
body:
Gorvokk
CR 13

This enormous, apelike beast has shaggy fur and a vicious underbite. Its arms end with three claws, two of them as large and sharp as any greatsword. The creature lets out an earth-shaking roar and pounds its massive chest, ready for combat.

XP 25,600
N Huge magical beast
Init +2; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +18

DEFENSE

AC 30, touch 11, flat-footed 27 (+2 Dex, +1 dodge, +19 natural, –2 size)
hp 175 (13d10+104)
Fort +16, Ref +10, Will +9

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., climb 20 ft.
Melee 2 claws +24 (4d6+12/19-20), bite +23 (2d8+12)
Space 15 ft.; Reach 15 ft.
Special Attacks armor-piercing claws, rend (2 claws, 4d6+24), terrifying roar

STATISTICS

Str 34, Dex 15, Con 26, Int 3, Wis 17, Cha 8
Base Atk +13; CMB +27; CMD 40
Feats Dodge, Improved Critical (claws), Improved Vital Strike, Iron Will, Power Attack, Vital Strike, Weapon Focus (claws)
Skills Climb +24, Perception +18
Languages Common (can’t speak)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Armor-Piercing Claws (Ex)

Claw attacks of a gorvokk ignore hardness and damage reduction. When attacking with its claws, a gorvokk treats its opponent’s armor and natural armor bonuses as 50% lower (rounded down, so a +9 armor bonus would become a +4 armor bonus).

Terrifying Roar (Su)

The terrifying roar of the gorvokk unnerves even the bravest souls. When a gorvokk roars (a standard action the creature can perform at will), all hearing creatures within a 300-foot spread must succeed on a DC 24 Will save or become panicked for 2d6 rounds and shaken for 1d10 minutes thereafter. Whether or not the save is successful, creatures in the area are immune to the roar of that gorvokk for 24 hours. This is a sonic, mind-affecting fear effect. The save DC is Constitution-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm hills
Organization solitary, pair, or family (3-6)
Treasure incidental

Gorvokks are among the ultimate predators of the arid uplands, looking like moving, furred mountains of muscle among the rocky hills. Gorvokks are powerful, fearless and fiercely territorial, willing to combat even creatures like dragons. Strong enough to crush rock, with a bite capable of mangling steel plate and a roar startling enough to frighten off a tribe of giants, they are powerful opponents. All those things would be enough to end most encounters, and yet pale before the greatest weapon of a gorvokk – its vicious claws. Gorvokks have three fingers on each hand, with the thumb being equipped with a smaller claw and fulfilling mostly an auxiliary role in most tasks. It is the claws on two other fingers that are the true reason for the legendary lethality of these beasts. Gorvokks are known to tear elephants in twain, their fearsome natural blades serving as a multiplier of their indomitable strength. Size and sharpness aren’t the only, or even the most impressive, attribute of their claws. For reasons unknown, these natural wonders are incredibly hard and nigh-unbreakable, which is likely the reason for their incredible sharpness. While the exact quality of this material varies between individuals, it rivals adamantine on average, allowing a gorvokk to effortlessly pierce dragon scales, metal armor and almost any other protection they encounter. While gorvokks are slightly smarter than primates and most are even capable of understanding at least one language, they are still closer to beasts than men and act accordingly. Gorvokks tend to live in small families, making their lairs in caverns which allow them to cool their massive bodies off away from the sun. Gorvokks eat all parts of their prey, so the caves in which they live have little evidence of their previous meals, except perhaps the permeating stench filling the air. In territories where gorvokks are either greater in number or real danger is more prevalent, the creatures sometimes band into larger clans consisting of multiple families. Gorvokks are occasionally recruited by more intelligent beings, most often being bribed with food by powerful humanoid tribes. Such alliances most often consist of a gorvokk being directed towards an enemy that needs to be destroyed, and then being paid inordinate amounts of meat as payment. Longer cooperation is rare, but on some occasions gorvokks will accept a tribe settling near their cavern, if the creatures are respectful and feed them well, as gorvokks will gladly choose bursts of activity and lazing around most of the time over regular hunting. While it is very rare on account of their strength and personality, gorvokks are sometimes forced into servitude by very powerful beings, like very old and powerful dragons, in which case they most often function similar to guard dogs in their master’s lair and eat scraps.

An average gorvokk is over 20 feet tall and weighs around 7 tons. Their fur is most often brownish, but some specimens exhibit gray or even black colors. Most gorvokks mature in 12 years and live for up to 80, although most are claimed by violence or misfortune much earlier than that. For poorly understood reasons, some specimens live much longer, and there are reports of gorvokks approaching their 200th winter still terrorizing their domains. Gorvokks lose little strength as they age, but lose color quickly, their fur starting to turn white in patches around 30 years of age and last vestiges of color disappearing around 50. Alpha individuals leading the individual families or clans are almost always large and already entirely bleached.

A gorvokk leader is best represented via the advanced simple template. Very rarely, gorvokks can gain class levels, most often in the barbarian class.
